summary: In this excerpt from a fiction work titled 'Book 4 — part 26', Felix, Van, and Rosa toast to rebuilding after a collapse, with Felix insisting they expand the network of people talking to each other and take care of one another. Rosa agrees to help on the condition that no one calls her Minister of Health or asks her to call them Prime Minister. The narrative then skips years ahead: Felix repeatedly rebuilds after groups fall apart, does manual work, and eventually takes a data-center job for a small government, with Van joining him. Life is hard and marked by sickness and tragedy, but Felix finds meaning in the data-center's hum.
one_line: Felix, Van and Rosa vow to rebuild a community after collapse, and the story follows Felix's hard, persistent years afterward.
key_facts: Felix says the group will expand 'this patch of the world where people are talking to each other' and take care of everyone they can find.
Felix says 'We'll probably fuck it up. We'll probably fail. I'd rather fail than give up, though.'
Van calls Felix 'crazier than Sario' and says Felix will drag Sario out first thing the next day.
Felix says 'Humans aren't the kind of things that have endings.'
Rosa agrees to help on the condition that she is never asked to call them Prime Minister and is never called Minister of Health.
Van says Felix 'prefers Prime Minister' in a stagey whisper.
The toast is 'To the world,' 'To humanity,' 'To rebuilding,' 'To anything,' and 'To everything.'
The group starts to rebuild the next day, then restarts months later after disagreements drive the fragile group apart, and again a year after that and five years after that.
Felix dug ditches, salvaged cans, buried the dead, planted and harvested, fixed cars, and learned to make biodiesel.
Felix ends up in a data-center for a little government that wanted to keep records, and Van goes with him.
Felix and Van spend time in chat rooms and meet old friends from the Distributed Republic of Cyberspace, who call him PM.
Felix's wounds never healed, and neither did most other people's; there were lingering and sudden sicknesses and tragedy on tragedy.
Felix likes the data-center because in the humming of the racks he never feels it is the first days or the last days of a better nation.
